TOBIAS VENKATARAMAN
Backend Engineer
Columbus, OH | tobias.venkataraman@example.com | (555) 014-2273 | github.com/tvenkat-example

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with about 6 years of experience building high-throughput services in Go and Kotlin on PostgreSQL and Kafka. Tech lead for Project Tern, the carrier-settlement rewrite at Larkspur Freight. Comfortable owning a service from design doc through launch and on-call.

Larkspur Freight | Software Engineer II, Backend | Columbus, OH | Mar 2023 - Present

- Cut p95 latency of the rate-quote API from 820 ms to 190 ms by replacing N+1 PostgreSQL queries with a batched loader and a 90-second Redis cache keyed by lane ID.
- Designed Dockhand, a Kafka event pipeline that processes about 2.3 million shipment status events per day, using a transactional outbox table to avoid duplicate writes.
- Reduced monthly settlement mismatches from 312 to 41 with a nightly reconciliation job that compares carrier invoices against booked loads.
- Partitioned the 1.9-billion-row load_events table by month in PostgreSQL, cutting nightly vacuum time from 4 hours to 35 minutes.
- Wrote the team's first set of 14 incident runbooks; member of a 6-person on-call rotation.

Quillfeather Health | Software Engineer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2021 - Feb 2023
- Built the appointment-reminder service in Kotlin (Spring Boot) that sent 11 million SMS and email reminders in 2022; the no-show rate at the 9 pilot clinics fell from 18.4% to 12.9%.
- Migrated 38 cron scripts into Metronome, a single Temporal-based scheduler, removing a class of double-send bugs.
- Introduced Pact contract tests between 5 internal services, cutting integration-environment breakages from roughly 9 per month to 2.
- Implemented field-level encryption for patient phone numbers using envelope keys in AWS KMS.

Brindlecap Labs | Junior Developer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2020 - Jul 2021
- Maintained a Python/Django inventory tool used by 60 independent bookstores; added a CSV import that replaced a manual 3-hour weekly task.
- Wrote the product's first automated test suite, taking line coverage from 0% to 71%.
- Handled customer-support escalations one day per week.

SIDE PROJECT
Sparrowhawk (open source, maintainer since 2022)
- Go library for idempotency keys backed by PostgreSQL advisory locks; about 640 GitHub stars.
- Supports configurable key expiry and a replay-safe response cache; test suite runs against PostgreSQL 13 through 16.

EDUCATION
Ohio Valley Polytechnic University | B.S. Computer Science, Minor in Mathematics | May 2020
- Senior capstone: a route-planning simulator for municipal snowplow fleets.

SKILLS
Languages: Go, Kotlin, Python, SQL, some TypeScript
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, AWS SQS
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS, KMS), Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, Datadog

PI-A:JD.title: the job description the user is targeting
PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

DTEAM-CTX-G1.text:
Orchard Mobile - Weekly Product Sync
Date: Thursday 17 September 2026, 10:00-10:45
Notes by: Lena Okafor (engineering lead)
Attendees: Hiro Tanaka (product manager), Lena Okafor, Priya Nand (backend), Marcus Oyelaran (mobile), Dana Whitfield (design), Tomas Reyes (QA)
Absent: Rafael Duarte (Platform team) - sent a written update

1. Release 2.4 dates (confirmed)
- Code freeze: Friday 9 October
- Beta to pilot customers: Wednesday 14 October
- General availability (GA): Wednesday 28 October
No change to dates this week. Hiro will re-check the dates at the 1 October sync.

2. Decisions
D1. CSV export of timesheets is OUT of scope for 2.4 and moves to 2.5. Reason: the Ledger API v5 bulk endpoint will not be ready before code freeze, and building export on v4 would mean doing the work twice. Proposed by Hiro, agreed by all attendees. - Push notifications for timesheet approvals. Marcus thinks it is a half-day job, Priya thinks it needs a backend queue. No decision; not in 2.4 unless someone brings a sized proposal.
- Release notes owner: unassigned. Hiro asked for a volunteer and nobody took it.

4. Status (short)
- Ledger v5 migration for pay-period endpoints: about 70% done (Priya).
- Offline clock-in: happy path works; conflict resolution (two devices clocking the same shift) not started (Marcus).
- Shift reminder screens: designs approved; copy still in review (Dana).
- QA: regression suite for Android 12-15 and iOS 17-19 being updated. Tomas is at 60% capacity because he is shared with the Web team until 5 October.

5. Action items
- Priya Nand: finish Ledger v5 migration for pay-period endpoints by Tue 29 Sep.
- Marcus Oyelaran: offline clock-in conflict resolution PR by Fri 2 Oct.
- Dana Whitfield: final shift-reminder copy and empty states by Wed 23 Sep.
- Tomas Reyes: updated regression suite ready by Mon 12 Oct.
- Hiro Tanaka: Kestrel contract signed by Thu 1 Oct; tell Brennan Foods about export moving to 2.5 by Fri 18 Sep.
- Lena Okafor: raise the Ledger API v5 bulk endpoint date with Rafael Duarte (Platform) by Fri 18 Sep.

6. Written update from Platform (Rafael Duarte)
Ledger API v5 bulk endpoints are targeted for Friday 2 October. Rafael described this date as "likely but not committed" and asked that nobody quote it to customers.

Next sync: Thursday 24 September, 10:00.

DTEAM-CTX-G2.title: Orchard Mobile 2.4 release plan and roadmap v1.3
DTEAM-CTX-G2.text:
Orchard Mobile 2.4 - Release Plan and Roadmap
Version 1.3 - owner Hiro Tanaka (PM) - last updated Friday 18 September 2026
Change log: v1.3 moves CSV export to 2.5 and records the Kestrel Messaging choice (both from the 17 September sync).

Goal
Release 2.4 makes Orchard usable for hourly teams who do not sit at a desk: shift reminders by SMS, clock-in that works without signal, and a clear pay-period summary.

In scope for 2.4
1. Shift reminders by SMS (Kestrel Messaging), opt-in per worker.
2. Offline clock-in behind feature flag offline_clockin_v1.
3. Pay-period summary screen (needs Ledger API v5).
4. Accessibility fixes to WCAG 2.2 AA on 14 screens.

Out of scope for 2.4
- CSV export of timesheets (moved to 2.5)
- Dark mode (2.6)
- Manager approval flow redesign (2.6)
- Apple Watch app (not planned)

Milestones
- Tue 29 Sep: pay-period endpoints migrated to Ledger v5 (Priya Nand)
- Fri 2 Oct: Platform ships Ledger API v5 bulk endpoints (external; owner Rafael Duarte)
- Mon 5 Oct: go/no-go on the Ledger fallback (Hiro Tanaka and Lena Okafor)
- Fri 9 Oct: code freeze
- Wed 14 Oct: beta to 400 pilot users across three customers: Brennan Foods (Ohio), Tidewater Clinics (Halifax, Canada), Marlow Transit (Oregon)
- Wed 28 Oct: GA, phased release over 7 days on both stores
- Wed 11 Nov: 2.5 planning kickoff

Dependencies
- Ledger API v5 bulk endpoints (Platform team). Needed by the pay-period summary.
- Kestrel Messaging contract (Procurement). Monthly SMS spend above $5,000 needs Finance sign-off; the current estimate is 1.2 million messages a month, about $8,500.
- Kestrel carrier registration for Canadian numbers takes up to 10 business days after the contract is signed. It is required before any Tidewater Clinics worker can receive SMS reminders.
- App store review: keep 3 business days of buffer before GA.

Risks and mitigations
R1. Ledger API v5 bulk endpoints slip past 2 October. Impact: the pay-period summary screen cannot load totals for pay periods longer than 14 days. Mitigation: fall back to the v4 read endpoints for 2.4 and show a "totals updating" state. The call is made at the 5 October go/no-go. If we fall back, the pay-period summary ships read-only.
R2. SMS deliverability in Canada if carrier registration is late. Mitigation: sign the contract by 1 October; reminders for Tidewater default to email until registration completes.
R3. QA capacity. Tomas Reyes is shared with the Web team until 5 October. Mitigation: a QA contractor for 2 weeks starting 5 October (budget approved by Lena Okafor).
R4. Offline clock-in data conflicts. Mitigation: the flag stays at 10% of beta users; full rollout only after conflict resolution passes regression.

Roles
- Accountable: Hiro Tanaka
- Engineering lead: Lena Okafor
- Backend: Priya Nand. Mobile: Marcus Oyelaran. Design: Dana Whitfield. QA: Tomas Reyes.

Success measures for beta
- Reminder opt-in: at least 40% of pilot workers
- Clock-in failures: under 0.5% of attempts
- Crash-free sessions: target to be agreed (see the 17 September sync)

Communication
Hiro owns all customer-facing communication about dates and scope. Engineers do not give dates to pilot customers directly.

Office Move FAQ - Harbor Street, 3rd floor
From: Workplace team

When is the move?
The move weekend is 12-13 December. Packing crates arrive on Tuesday 8 December. Please have your desk packed by 5pm on Friday 11 December.

Where are we going?
Third floor of the Harbor Street building, same address, different lift. The kitchen is on the east side and there are two new phone booths by the stairwell.

Do I keep my desk?
No. The third floor uses bookable desks. Book through the Deskly app up to 14 days ahead. Team neighbourhoods are marked by colour; Product and Engineering are in the green zone.

IT will move monitors and docks for you. Label cables with the stickers in your crate. Personal items are your responsibility.

Parking?
Parking permits carry over. Bike storage moves to the basement cage; request a new fob from reception.

Who do I contact?
Workplace team at the front desk, or the #office-move channel.

items.question: they want me to take the Ledger migration AND keep all my sprint commitments. what do I push back with, what do I offer instead, and how do I say it without sounding like I'm dodging?
items.answer: I'd take the migration, but I'd be straight that both at once means one of them slips. So I'd ask which matters more right now, and offer a real trade: I own the migration and hand off or push a couple of sprint items, or I keep the sprint and take the migration on a longer timeline. Then I'd name what I need to make it work, like a clear priority order and someone to pick up the handoffs. That's not dodging, it's making the choice explicit so we decide it together instead of me quietly failing at both.
